open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 and M04 ResourceBounds
open_points.text: “ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` (address space, each scratch file's size, processes)” calls scratch-file size a ResourceBounds limit, but M04 contains only `wall_time_ms`, `memory_bytes`, `output_bytes` and `process_count`; rule 1 instead names the release constant `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: Is the scratch-file limit always the release-wide `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, or must ResourceBounds gain a per-contract scratch-file field?
options: Use the release-wide `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`
Add a scratch-file field to M04
Derive the limit from another existing M04 field

open_points.subject: A03 scratch storage bound
open_points.text: “one private exchange directory in which every file the code writes is bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`” limits each file but says nothing about the number of files or their aggregate bytes.
open_points.question: May one execution create arbitrarily many individually conforming scratch files, or is the exchange directory also subject to an aggregate byte or file-count limit?
options: Only each individual file is bounded
The directory has an aggregate byte limit
Both aggregate bytes and file count are bounded
open_points.default_guess: Apply `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` as an aggregate directory limit as well as a per-file limit.

open_points.subject: A03 process_count enforcement
open_points.text: “processes” replaces the former rule that set the in-namespace process limit “at `process_count` plus one” but does not say what the new `process_count` counts.
open_points.question: Does `process_count` include the already-running sandbox runner, and what exact RLIMIT_NPROC value must be installed?
options: Set RLIMIT_NPROC to `process_count` and count the runner
Set it to `process_count + 1` so the bound counts child processes
Define `process_count` as all processes in the execution including infrastructure
open_points.default_guess: Treat `process_count` as the total number of in-environment processes, including the runner, and set RLIMIT_NPROC to that value.

open_points.subject: A03 limit installation boundary
open_points.text: “set inside the environment before the code loads” does not say whether resource consumption by bubblewrap, the in-sandbox runner, interpreter startup, imported standard-library modules or child processes counts against the contract bounds.
open_points.question: Exactly which sandbox and runner processes and which phases of their lifetime are charged to `memory_bytes`, `process_count` and the scratch-file limit?
options: Charge only user code after module loading begins
Charge the runner and every descendant once limits are installed
Charge bubblewrap and all setup as well as the runner and descendants
open_points.default_guess: Charge the runner and every descendant from immediately before the implementation module is loaded.

open_points.subject: A03 resource-exhaustion classification
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`” does not define when a setrlimit-enforced scratch, memory or process limit counts as hit, particularly when Python receives and catches `OSError`, `MemoryError` or a signal and then returns conforming output.
open_points.question: Must any attempted operation rejected by one of these limits irreversibly classify the execution as `resource_exhausted`, even if the implementation catches the resulting exception, and how is that hit observed?
options: Any rejected operation latches `resource_exhausted`
Only abnormal termination attributable to the limit counts
A caught limit error permits successful completion
open_points.default_guess: Latch any observed limit rejection and return `resource_exhausted`, even if user code catches it.

open_points.subject: A03 scratch failure classification
open_points.text: The outcome order names “scratch” as a limit hit, but the text does not distinguish reaching `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` from host filesystem exhaustion, inode exhaustion, quota failure or another exchange-directory write error.
open_points.question: Which scratch write failures are `resource_exhausted`, and which are `crashed` or ordinary exceptions visible to the implementation?
options: Every capacity-related scratch write failure is `resource_exhausted`
Only exceeding the configured file-size limit is `resource_exhausted`
All scratch I/O failures are `crashed` unless caught by the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Classify configured-limit, filesystem-capacity, inode and quota exhaustion as `resource_exhausted`; classify other I/O faults as `crashed`.

open_points.subject: A03 start probe
open_points.text: Rule 8 still requires that “one probe execution succeeds,” but the changed rule removed the requirement that the probe set every limit at the current release ceilings in the same way as real executions.
open_points.question: Which limits and values must the start probe install, and must startup fail if any release-ceiling limit cannot be installed?
options: Probe every limit at the current release ceilings
Probe representative fixed values
Probe only that bubblewrap and Python can execute
open_points.default_guess: Probe every enforcement mechanism at the current release ceilings and refuse startup if any cannot be installed.

open_points.subject: A03 sandbox responsibility clause
open_points.text: “and with the parent's own wall deadline and output count; how is the sandbox's own (decision 30).”
open_points.question: What subject is governed by “how is the sandbox's own”: the choice of enforcement mechanism, the implementation of all limits, or some other behavior, and which observable requirements does decision 30 impose?
options: Only enforcement mechanics are sandbox-private while all stated outcomes remain normative
All resource-limit details are delegated to the sandbox
Restore the omitted wording from decision 30
open_points.default_guess: Treat only the internal enforcement mechanism as sandbox-private and keep every stated bound, precedence and outcome normative.
